videos.title: पहले यह जान लो: पैसा, bank और payment की बुनियाद
videos.goal: Learner खरीद और उधार, balance और loan, रकम और purchasing power, institutions और payment instructions के सीधे फर्क examples से समझेगा।
prerequisites_taught: Purchases, prices, debts and payments due later
Bank balances, deposits, loans and interest
Denominations, monetary arithmetic, percentages and minimum–maximum limits
Purchasing power, inflation, scarcity and liquidity
Central bank, commercial bank, government treasury and bank-to-bank settlement
Foreign currencies, exchange rates, reserves and demand–supply changes
Chronological reading: BCE/CE, centuries, dynasties and law versus implementation dates
Digital instructions, identity authentication, ledgers and payment interfaces
videos.opening_hook: दुकान से सामान अभी मिला, पैसे कल देने हैं—क्या खरीद और payment एक ही समय हुए?
videos.story_or_analogy: Outside, standard textbook-level teaching examples: दुकान का उधार purchase और debt अलग करेगा; account में जमा रकम और borrowed रकम balance, loan और interest समझाएँगे। ₹100 का 2% और minimum–maximum की छोटी calculation होगी। एक ही रकम से कम सामान मिलना purchasing power, तुरंत खर्च हो सकना liquidity समझाएगा। 2 banks के customers का payment institutions और settlement अलग करेगा। Currency exchange का छोटा example exchange rate और reserves खोलेगा। छोटी timeline BCE/CE, century और law–implementation का फर्क बताएगी। App पर instruction, PIN से पहचान की जाँच और ledger में entry को अलग actions की तरह दिखाएँगे।
videos.why_this_unit: यही सीधे इस्तेमाल होने वाली बुनियाद है; हर prerequisite को छोटे explanation और example से सिखाएँगे, उसके पीछे का अलग syllabus नहीं खोलेंगे।

videos.title: Money क्या है, और हमारे कौन-से काम करता है?
videos.goal: Learner acceptance-based definition, scope और characteristics समझेगा; 4 functions को overview से लेकर examples, boundaries और comparison तक पहचान सकेगा।
videos.opening_hook: आपके पास कोई कीमती चीज़ है, लेकिन दुकानदार उसे payment में नहीं लेता—क्या वह आपके लिए money है?
videos.story_or_analogy: एक खरीद में price बताना, payment करना, रकम बचाना और बाद की payment तय करना अलग situations होंगे। पहले situations समझेंगे, फिर 4 functions के नाम और definitions जोड़ेंगे; गैर-उदाहरण से boundaries जाँचेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Money की पहचान और उसके काम साथ समझने पर cash को ही पूरा money मानने की गलती टूटती है।

videos.title: Barter से commodity money: बदलाव की ज़रूरत क्यों पड़ी?
videos.goal: Learner barter की अलग-अलग limitations, schematic evolution, intrinsic–extrinsic value और commodity money के examples, फायदे तथा सीमाएँ समझेगा।
videos.opening_hook: आपके पास अनाज है और आपको जूते चाहिए—लेकिन जूते वाले को अनाज नहीं चाहिए। सौदा कैसे होगा?
videos.story_or_analogy: Outside illustrative exchange में दोनों लोगों की जरूरतें मिलाने की कोशिश पहले दिखाएँगे। फिर double coincidence और दूसरी limitations अलग करेंगे। किसी वस्तु के अपने उपयोग और payment value को अलग रखकर commodity family के region–use examples, strengths और weaknesses की comparison करेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: समस्या, बदलाव का broad क्रम और value का फर्क मिलकर समझाते हैं कि commodity money क्यों आया और वह अंतिम समाधान क्यों नहीं था।

videos.title: Metallic money और भारत के शुरुआती coins
videos.goal: Learner commodity से metallic money और फिर paper की जरूरत तक causal links समझेगा; शुरुआती Indian coinage का पूरा supplied क्रम और dynasty–coinage pairings पढ़ सकेगा।
videos.opening_hook: छोटी खरीद में coin सुविधाजनक है, लेकिन बहुत बड़ी रकम साथ ले जानी हो तो क्या दिक्कत आएगी?
videos.story_or_analogy: पहले छोटी और बड़ी payment में metallic money की उपयोगिता तथा सीमा समझेंगे। फिर Indian metallic-money examples को dated timeline पर रखेंगे; chronology और matching की अलग जाँच होगी।
videos.why_this_unit: Metallic money का mechanism और उसके Indian examples साथ रखने से इतिहास केवल names की list नहीं रहेगा।

videos.title: Paper money, fiat money और legal tender का फर्क
videos.goal: Learner gold-backed paper के milestones, fiat money के meaning और currency examples समझेगा; legal tender, commemorative coins, acceptance limits और payment instruments की boundaries अलग कर सकेगा।
videos.opening_hook: एक note का material सस्ता है, फिर भी उससे सामान मिलता है—क्या वजह केवल उसके पीछे रखा gold है?
videos.story_or_analogy: पहले redeemable paper claim और material से अलग monetary value की situations आएँगी। फिर historical sequence, fiat definition और legal acceptance की अलग comparison होगी। Coin denomination और कुल payment limit को अलग पढ़ेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Backing, value और legal status जुड़े हुए हैं, लेकिन एक ही बात नहीं हैं; इन्हें साथ पढ़ना मुख्य exam confusion दूर करता है।

videos.title: Gold link टूटा, फिर भी dollar की माँग क्यों रही?
videos.goal: Learner Bretton Woods का US$35 gold link, Triffin contradiction, 1971 decision और petrodollars से continuing dollar demand की causal chains समझेगा।
videos.opening_hook: दुनिया को trade के लिए और dollars चाहिए, लेकिन हर dollar के gold में बदलने का भरोसा भी चाहिए—तनाव कहाँ बनेगा?
videos.story_or_analogy: Dollar availability और gold-conversion confidence को 2 अलग जरूरतों की तरह दिखाएँगे। हर causal link के बाद उसका नतीजा जोड़ेंगे; gold link समाप्त होने और dollar demand समाप्त होने को अलग रखेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: International monetary व्यवस्था का turning point और उसके बाद dollar demand एक लगातार कहानी बनाते हैं।

videos.title: Rupee की यात्रा: पुराने coins से Digital Rupee तक
videos.goal: Learner rupee origins, standardisation, colonial laws और institutions का क्रम समझेगा; independent rupee के decimalisation, exchange regime और symbol को अलग करेगा तथा wholesale–retail Digital Rupee pilots की comparison कर सकेगा।
videos.opening_hook: आज ₹1 को 100 पैसे में गिनते हैं—क्या rupee की गिनती और व्यवस्था हमेशा ऐसी ही थी?
videos.story_or_analogy: एक timeline पर origins, colonial standardisation और independent reforms के अलग sections होंगे। Laws, committees, coin-metal pairs और institutions को उनके काम से जोड़ेंगे। अंत में Digital Rupee family का wholesale–retail comparison होगा, और bank balance तथा UPI से उसकी boundary साफ करेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: एक ही currency की continuity में historical milestones और नए digital form को जोड़ने से dates और functions अलग-अलग समझ आते हैं।

videos.title: Tughlaq की token currency: भरोसा कहाँ टूटा?
videos.goal: Learner पूरे historical case में token value, credibility, counterfeiting, state control और treasury consequences के links समझेगा।
videos.opening_hook: सरकार किसी token की value तय कर दे, लेकिन वैसा token कोई भी बना सके—फिर लोग क्या करेंगे?
videos.story_or_analogy: Historical case को decision, acceptance की शर्तें, control की समस्या, लोगों की प्रतिक्रिया और परिणाम के क्रम में खोलेंगे। Intrinsic value और token value को दोबारा पूरी तरह पढ़ाए बिना case में लागू करेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: यह विस्तृत case trust और legal declaration के बीच की दूरी दिखाता है; इसे स्वतंत्र समय देना जरूरी है।

videos.title: Note पहचानना, उसका promise समझना और MANI
videos.goal: Learner banknote features के identification, accessibility और security functions समझेगा; ₹1-note exception, language counts, promise clause, bearer status और legal promissory-note distinction अलग करेगा; MANI का काम और उसकी सीमा समझेगा।
videos.opening_hook: Note पर लिखे promise का मतलब क्या हर बार उतना ही सामान मिलना है—और note देख न पाने वाला व्यक्ति उसकी denomination कैसे पहचाने?
videos.story_or_analogy: Note का fixed visual reading path होगा: पहचान, accessibility, security और issuer/signatory। फिर promise को face value, purchasing power और gold redemption की अलग comparisons से खोलेंगे। MANI के पहचानने वाले काम को authenticity जाँच मानने की गलती से अलग करेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: एक physical note के design, legal meaning और accessibility tool को साथ देखने से हर feature का अलग उद्देश्य स्पष्ट होता है।

videos.title: Note वापस लेना, demonetisation और Gresham's Law
videos.goal: Learner withdrawal और demonetisation का legal फर्क समझेगा; selective spending से Gresham's Law का mechanism और उसकी आवश्यक conditions पहचान सकेगा।
videos.opening_hook: किसी note को circulation से वापस लिया जाए, तो क्या उसी क्षण उससे payment करना गैरकानूनी हो जाता है?
videos.story_or_analogy: पहले withdrawal और legal-tender status को अलग decisions की तरह तुलना करेंगे। फिर समान तय payment value वाली, लेकिन अलग material value वाली coins की स्थिति में spending और holding का चुनाव चलाएँगे; उसके बाद law का नाम और limits आएँगी।
videos.why_this_unit: दोनों concepts में legal status और लोगों का व्यवहार अलग करके देखना जरूरी है; slogan से गलत निष्कर्ष नहीं निकालेंगे।

videos.title: Bank money, cheque, demand draft और overdraft
videos.goal: Learner negotiable instruments की पूरी family, promise–order, parties और cheque dishonour समझेगा; prepaid demand draft, credit-based overdraft तथा MICR–IFSC के formats और uses अलग कर सकेगा।
videos.opening_hook: Account में पैसा होना और किसी को cheque देना—क्या दोनों का मतलब payment पूरा हो जाना है?
videos.story_or_analogy: एक payment situation में promise करने वाला, order देने वाला और payment पाने वाला अलग दिखेंगे। Family overview के बाद हर instrument को समान criteria पर पढ़ेंगे। Demand draft और overdraft में funding का समय, available credit और इस्तेमाल पर interest अलग होंगे; codes को cheque processing और electronic routing के काम से जोड़ेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Money के claim, उसे transfer करने के instruction और credit facility का फर्क एक coherent banking unit में समझ आता है।

videos.title: UPI payment के पीछे कौन क्या करता है?
videos.goal: Learner RBI, NPCI, banks और customer-facing providers की roles अलग करेगा; UPI routing, initiation, authorisation, push–pull और delegated payments को step by step समझेगा।
videos.opening_hook: आपने app पर payment किया—पैसा app के पास था, NPCI के पास था या bank में?
videos.story_or_analogy: एक दुकान payment पहले सफल result से खुलेगा, फिर instruction का route, जरूरी participants और authorisation की conditions दिखाई जाएँगी। Push, pull और delegation के अलग runs होंगे; किसी जरूरी step के न होने पर payment क्यों रुकता है, यह भी स्पष्ट होगा।
videos.why_this_unit: पहले institutions का map और फिर उसी map पर transaction चलाने से app, network और underlying money नहीं मिलेंगे।

videos.title: NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI—और AePS, BBPS
videos.goal: Learner settlement, availability, limits और charges की दिशा पर payment systems की comparison करेगा; AePS की inclusion भूमिका और BBPS के bill-payment काम को अलग पहचान सकेगा।
videos.opening_hook: बड़ी रकम भेजनी हो, तुरंत छोटा payment करना हो या bill भरना हो—क्या हर जरूरत के लिए वही system चुनेंगे?
videos.story_or_analogy: पहले अलग payment needs आएँगी, फिर एक criterion पर सभी relevant systems साथ रखेंगे। Settlement का तरीका, operating hours, amount limits और inward–outward charges को अलग rows में पढ़ेंगे; AePS और BBPS को उनके काम की situations से पहचानेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: एक साथ comparison करने से system names याद करने के बजाय सही criteria पर statement जाँचना आएगा।

videos.title: RuPay, e-RUPI और merchant को मिलने वाली रकम
videos.goal: Learner RuPay card types, domestic role और overseas links समझेगा; e-RUPI की beneficiary–purpose restrictions और MDR के payer, recipients तथा gross–net calculation को अलग कर सकेगा।
videos.opening_hook: Customer ने पूरा payment किया, फिर merchant के account में उससे कम रकम क्यों आ सकती है?
videos.story_or_analogy: पहले card family का overview और types की समान criteria पर comparison होगी। फिर purpose-bound voucher की situation से e-RUPI समझेंगे। Supplied 2% MDR example में gross amount से fee और net receipt निकालकर fee distribution के participants जोड़ेंगे; voucher को Digital Rupee या खुली cash payment नहीं मानेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Card network, restricted voucher और payment fee अलग layers हैं; साथ पढ़ने से पैसे, product और charge का फर्क साफ होगा।

videos.title: Cross-border payments, polymer notes और cryptocurrency
videos.goal: Learner Project Nexus की जरूरत, leadership, participating systems और country–system matching समझेगा; polymer notes के material–durability claims और cryptocurrency के distributed ownership records को fiat तथा CBDC से अलग करेगा।
videos.opening_hook: अपने देश में payment तुरंत हो जाता है—दूसरे देश के fast-payment system तक पहुँचने में अलग समस्या क्यों आती है?
videos.story_or_analogy: पहले national payment systems को जोड़ने की जरूरत से Nexus का mechanism खुलेगा। फिर स्पष्ट topic transition के साथ 3 अलग बदलाव रखेंगे: payment connectivity, note का material और ownership record की व्यवस्था। Polymer तथा crypto को एक जैसी monetary category नहीं बताएँगे।
videos.why_this_unit: ये नए बदलाव अलग सवाल हल करते हैं; अलग comparisons और छोटा closing recap उन्हें digital money के एक अस्पष्ट label में मिलने से रोकेंगे।

videos.title: Money supply: M0 से M4 तक क्या गिना जाता है?
videos.goal: Learner aggregate overview से M0–M4 की पूरी family समझेगा; formulas को component by component बनाएगा और currency in circulation, public currency, RBI deposits, demand deposits, time deposits तथा post-office coverage की boundaries पहचान सकेगा।
videos.opening_hook: जेब का cash, bank balance और fixed deposit—देश का money गिनते समय क्या सबको हर बार एक ही total में जोड़ेंगे?
videos.story_or_analogy: पहले अलग जगह रखी रकम की situation, फिर मापने की जरूरत और aggregate names आएँगे। Overview के बाद M0 का base अलग समझाएँगे; M1–M4 को component cards से बनाएँगे। M1–M2 और M3–M4 की direct comparison, liquidity, NSC exclusion और inclusion–exclusion checks होंगे; M0 को बाकी aggregates की सीधी nested सीढ़ी नहीं दिखाएँगे।
videos.why_this_unit: पूरी family एक video में रहने से formulas रटने के बजाय हर addition और exclusion का meaning समझ आएगा।

videos.title: PYQ अभ्यास: blockchain, RTGS–NEFT और BHIM
videos.goal: Learner supplied questions के हर statement और option का कारण सहित निर्णय करेगा; blockchain applications और permission, settlement–charges–hours तथा BHIM interoperability और authentication की traps अलग पहचान सकेगा।
videos.opening_hook: किसी statement का पहला हिस्सा सही हो, लेकिन आखिरी शब्द गलत हो—क्या आप उसे फिर भी सही चुनेंगे?
videos.story_or_analogy: हर supplied PYQ में पहले learner का निर्णय, फिर statement को छोटे claims में तोड़कर mechanism से जाँच होगी। Blockchain का ledger structure और applications जोड़ेंगे; technology को cryptocurrency तक सीमित नहीं करेंगे। Pre'25 wording में charge direction और hours, तथा BHIM में authentication factors और transaction steps अलग जाँचेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: पहले सीखे digital concepts को अब वास्तविक supplied statement combinations पर लागू करेंगे; recap के नाम पर नए PYQ content को नहीं छोड़ेंगे।

videos.title: PYQ अभ्यास: NPCI, inclusion, RuPay और MDR
videos.goal: Learner दोनों pages में फैले NPCI question को पूरा हल करेगा; inclusion और RuPay संबंधों का कारण समझेगा तथा MDR को merchant charge, incentive, cashback और government support से अलग कर सकेगा।
videos.opening_hook: Digital payment पर cashback मिले और merchant से fee कटे—क्या दोनों को MDR कह सकते हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: Continued NPCI question को एक पूरे question की तरह रखेंगे; हर claim और option की role–function जाँच होगी। MDR में पहले कौन किसे रकम देता है यह तय करेंगे, फिर definition और सभी distractors का कारण खोलेंगे। अंत में money, legal status, payment route और money supply के फर्क का एक closing recap होगा।
videos.why_this_unit: अंतिम application unit institutions और payment costs के सबसे सीधे exam confusions सुलझाकर chapter पूरा करता है।

plan.chapter_flow: v0 में 8 सीधे prerequisites examples से सिखेंगे। v1–v3 money की पहचान, जरूरत और शुरुआती forms बनाएँगे। v4–v7 backing, legal status, international व्यवस्था, rupee history और credibility को जोड़ेंगे। v8–v10 physical notes से banking claims और instruments तक जाएँगे। v11–v14 institutions, transaction routes, payment products और नए बदलाव अलग करेंगे। v15 पूरी money-supply family को साथ समझाएगा। v16–v17 supplied PYQs के हर statement और option को कारण सहित हल करेंगे। Topic narration कुल 149 minutes है; prerequisite सहित 157 minutes।

videos.title: पहले यह जान लो: पैसा, bank और payment की बुनियाद

frame.process: Distinguish buying goods, stating a price, owing money and paying.
frame.how: Follow a purchase on credit from delivery to repayment.
frame.when: Goods arrive today; payment is due tomorrow.
frame.conditions: The seller agrees to delayed payment.
frame.atmosphere: An everyday neighbourhood shop.

frame.process: Separate deposited funds, account balance, borrowing and interest.
frame.how: Track a deposit and a separate loan obligation.
frame.when: Deposit first, then borrowing and repayment over time.
frame.conditions: Interest depends on the agreed rate and period.
frame.atmosphere: A learner checking a bank account.

frame.process: Read denominations, amounts, percentages and transaction boundaries.
frame.how: Build equal totals and calculate a hypothetical percentage fee.
frame.when: Before comparing amounts or interpreting payment rules.
frame.conditions: Minimum and maximum are inclusive unless the wording specifies otherwise.
frame.atmosphere: Counting notes and reading a sample payment rule.

frame.process: Separate the amount held from buying capacity and spending readiness.
frame.how: Compare quantities bought, scarce goods and readily usable assets.
frame.when: Prices change or money is needed immediately.
frame.conditions: General price rises differ from an isolated price increase.
frame.atmosphere: A market visit and an urgent household payment.

frame.process: Distinguish customer banking, central banking, treasury and interbank settlement.
frame.how: Follow a payment between customers of two banks.
frame.when: Customer instructions lead to account changes and settlement between banks.
frame.conditions: Customer records and interbank obligations are separate layers.
frame.atmosphere: Two banks within India's monetary system.

frame.process: Understand currency conversion, exchange-rate movements and reserves.
frame.how: Compare the rupee cost of the same dollar amount at two hypothetical rates.
frame.when: Foreign payments create demand for another currency.
frame.conditions: Demand effects are explained with other influences held unchanged.
frame.atmosphere: An Indian buyer paying a foreign seller.

frame.process: Order historical periods and distinguish legal dates from implementation.
frame.how: Read BCE/CE markers, century boundaries and illustrative policy dates.
frame.when: Moving from ancient monetary history to modern reforms.
frame.conditions: Dates refer to different events; dynasties denote ruling families rather than single years.
frame.atmosphere: A simple historical timeline.

frame.process: Separate a payment interface, instruction, authentication and account record.
frame.how: Follow an illustrative digital payment from entry to recorded transfer.
frame.when: Details are entered, permission checked and records updated.
frame.conditions: An instruction or screenshot alone does not establish completed payment.
frame.atmosphere: A customer paying a shop through a phone.

beats.say: 2 packets हों और 10 लोग चाहें—जरूरत के मुकाबले यह कमी scarcity है; price पर ऊपर जाने का दबाव पड़ सकता है। आज ₹500 देने हों, तो cash तैयार है, जमीन तुरंत बेचना कठिन। बिना बड़ी कीमत घटाए asset को खर्च लायक बनाने की आसानी liquidity है; यह कितना खरीद सकते हो, उससे अलग है।

videos.title: Money क्या है, और हमारे कौन-से काम करता है?

frame.process: Recognise money by accepted payment use and explain five practical characteristics.
frame.how: Run concrete transactions first, define their shared qualities, then test boundaries.
frame.when: At purchase, repayment, repeated circulation, movement between shops and making change.
frame.conditions: Recipients accept payment; equivalent units are compared within the same denomination.
frame.atmosphere: Familiar neighbourhood shops, market stalls and a tea counter.

frame.process: Expand money beyond physical currency to accepted balances.
frame.how: Compare cash and balance-based payment for the same purchase.
frame.when: When a payment is completed without handing over notes or coins.
frame.conditions: The monetary balance is accepted for payment; the device is not itself money.
frame.atmosphere: A shop counter offering cash and non-cash payment.

skipped_steps.why: The source contains no formula to build.

frame.process: Explain how excessive spending against unchanged goods can reduce purchasing power.
frame.how: Compare total spending, basket prices and purchases possible with a fixed sum.
frame.when: After spending rises while the quantity of goods stays unchanged.
frame.conditions: Ten identical baskets sell at one price using all assumed spending; this is not a general proportional forecast.
frame.atmosphere: A simplified local grocery market with explicitly hypothetical numbers.

frame.process: Distinguish exchange, common valuation, carrying resources forward and specifying future dues.
frame.how: Run four situations before naming and defining the functions, then test confusing pairs.
frame.when: At purchase, before purchase, between income and spending, and when future repayments are agreed.
frame.conditions: Separate physical endurance from purchasing power and saved resources from obligations.
frame.atmosphere: Grocery and electronics shops, a salary account and a home-loan schedule.

videos.title: Paper money, fiat money और legal tender: 3 अलग सवाल

frame.process: A paper claim represents a fixed gold entitlement.
frame.how: The issuer returns gold when the holder presents the redeemable note.
frame.when: Under a historical gold-redemption arrangement, on demand.
frame.conditions: A credible fixed-gold redemption promise is required.
frame.atmosphere: A hypothetical bank counter, not today's Indian rupee system.

frame.process: Gold backing constrains additional note issue.
frame.how: Additional claims require supporting gold under the illustrative arrangement.
frame.when: Reserves support issue before redemption is demanded.
frame.conditions: The fully backed arithmetic is illustrative, not a historical reserve ratio.
frame.atmosphere: A bank balances gold stock against promised claims.

frame.process: Selected milestones trace paper claims, state authority and changing gold links.
frame.how: Chronological markers distinguish receipts, state notes, compulsory acceptance and monetary anchors.
frame.when: From Tang receipts in the 7th century to the 1971 endpoint.
frame.conditions: Geographical scope and official versus household redemption must remain distinct.
frame.atmosphere: Chinese and European developments join the international dollar-gold transition.

skipped_steps.why: The supplied milestones name authorities and arrangements but provide no individual decision-makers or choices.

frame.process: Fiat money supports purchases without commodity redemption.
frame.how: Government authority and confidence in continued acceptance support monetary value.
frame.when: A seller accepts payment expecting to spend it again.
frame.conditions: Material value, purchasing power and gold convertibility are different.
frame.atmosphere: A modern Indian kirana purchase.

frame.process: Fiat characteristics and currency examples identify value, governance and international use.
frame.how: Separate printing, authorised issuance and monetary-policy influence; identify currencies by codes.
frame.when: Modern fiat systems, with historical and undated captions qualified.
frame.conditions: No gold backing does not mean no regulation or no purchasing power.
frame.atmosphere: Indian monetary institutions and international currency markets.

skipped_steps.why: No formula is supplied for these characteristics or currency captions.

frame.process: Recognised currency settles obligations, with or without aggregate tender ceilings.
frame.how: Legal status and denomination determine payment capacity; circulation designs do not change denomination.
frame.when: Existing monetary obligations are settled using genuine, valid money.
frame.conditions: Applicable territory, legal rules and amount limits govern the result.
frame.atmosphere: Indian grocery debt settlements using notes and coins.

frame.process: Coin categories and denomination limits determine recognised payment use.
frame.how: Check issue status, total rupee value and whether acceptance is compulsory or voluntary.
frame.when: At payment; historical coins may retain collector value after losing tender status.
frame.conditions: Commemorative purpose does not establish universal tender status.
frame.atmosphere: A change drawer, Government Mint collector sets and an old household coin collection.

frame.process: Bitcoin illustrates changing legal payment status without sovereign fiat issuance.
frame.how: Legal recognition changes acceptance rules rather than the network's issuance system.
frame.when: The supplied account contrasts status through 2024 with practical changes after 2025 reforms.
frame.conditions: Ownership, voluntary use and compulsory acceptance must be distinguished.
frame.atmosphere: El-Salvador's dated Bitcoin example.

skipped_steps.why: No individual policymakers or personal choices are supplied.

frame.process: One coin carries different monetary and collector valuations.
frame.how: Payment uses denomination; a collector's voluntary purchase uses a market price.
frame.when: The coin is spent as money versus sold as a collectible.
frame.conditions: Collector premiums do not rewrite face value or aggregate tender limits.
frame.atmosphere: A valid ₹100 silver commemorative coin.

frame.process: Fee payments distinguish currency from instruments accessing deposits or credit.
frame.how: Successful cheque clearing transfers funds; card settlement creates repayment liability.
frame.when: Alternative routes for a hypothetical ₹1,000 fee.
frame.conditions: Acceptance arrangements and successful settlement are required.
frame.atmosphere: A college fee counter and the connected banking arrangements.

last_problems: [reviewer] b29–b30: The narration points at source presentation instead of teaching the facts: 'supplied figure', 'इन descriptions', and the incomplete 'second-most' caption. This violates W-01 even though the underlying caution is appropriate. -> fix: Teach directly that the historical count is 20 of 27, so EU membership and euro adoption differ. State that no specified measure supports an additional ranking, without discussing a caption. Replace the existing wording rather than adding time.

[reviewer] c09.3, b13–b15: Several timeline milestones are dates plus translated labels. In particular, compulsory acceptance and the gold-standard/dollar-gold anchors are named without explaining the need and causal significance. The required timeline step 'events in order with their causes' is not fulfilled or validly skipped. -> fix: Explain how compulsory acceptance differs from willingness, why a fixed gold quantity supplies a monetary reference, and why the international arrangement used the dollar-gold anchor. Mark these standard contextual explanations as outside knowledge. Cut generic recaps in b5, b18 and b22 to make room; preserve all dates.

[reviewer] c10.2, b27 and b31: International reserves remain an unopened technical label. Saying that a reserve currency can be fiat does not explain what reserves are or how a currency can serve that role without backing its own notes with gold. -> fix: Explain reserves as foreign-currency assets held for external payments, then distinguish holding foreign currency from promising gold redemption. Replace part of the generic b31 recap and trim repeated symbol identification to fund this explanation.

[reviewer] b42: UNC is expanded to 'Uncirculated' but its meaning is not actually taught. Preserving condition does not by itself explain that the coin has not circulated in everyday payments. -> fix: Replace the acronym-only expansion with 'UNC यानी Uncirculated—रोज़ के लेन-देन में नहीं चला coin'. Trim the repeated collector-purpose wording in the same beat.

frame.process: Trace the gold–Dollar arrangement from 1944 to the termination of convertibility in 1971.
frame.how: Explain the original anchor, accumulating pressures and Nixon's decision.
frame.when: 1944, the 1960s and 15 August 1971, in that order.
frame.conditions: Confidence depends on the credibility of the official gold-conversion promise.
frame.atmosphere: International trade needs usable balances while official holders seek dependable backing.

frame.process: Explain the conversion rate and the Dollar's reserve-currency role.
frame.how: Build conversion arithmetic and distinguish reserve assets from payments using them.
frame.when: Under the historical gold-linked arrangement, before the 1971 break.
frame.conditions: Conversion applied mainly to foreign central banks; numerical transactions are hypothetical.
frame.atmosphere: French and US authorities settle gold claims and machinery payments through banks.

frame.process: Explain why increasing external Dollar claims strained confidence in gold redemption.
frame.how: Compare the gold needed for claims with available gold, then contrast liquidity with confidence.
frame.when: Pressures accumulated by the 1960s, before the 1971 decision.
frame.conditions: The conflict appears when external claims grow without sufficient growth in gold.
frame.atmosphere: Trade expands while official holders worry about the conversion promise.

frame.process: Read the gold–Dollar–other currencies hierarchy.
frame.how: Trace the three boxes and two arrows from top to bottom.
frame.when: Read as a relationship within the arrangement, not a chronology.
frame.conditions: Arrows indicate monetary links, not physical gold shipments or retail conversion rights.
frame.atmosphere: A three-level diagram connects a familiar Rupee to the international monetary anchor.

frame.process: Connect the 1973 oil shock with the 1974 Saudi–US understanding.
frame.how: Explain restricted supply, higher prices, Saudi financial commitments and US security commitments.
frame.when: 1973 precedes the 1974 understanding.
frame.conditions: Pricing and investment are separate commitments; illustrative allocations are not historical shares.
frame.atmosphere: Oil importers face expensive supplies while Saudi Arabia and the US exchange financial and security commitments.

frame.process: Explain continuing Dollar demand from oil-payment requirements.
frame.how: Follow an enlarged Dollar invoice through a bank into payment demand.
frame.when: After gold convertibility ends, whenever oil invoices require Dollars.
frame.conditions: Dollar pricing is neither oil redemption nor a guarantee of exchange-value stability.
frame.atmosphere: An Indian oil importer obtains foreign currency to pay a seller.

frame.process: Answer why Dollars could still be held without gold backing.
frame.how: Apply the distinction between redemption backing and transaction demand.
frame.when: After teaching the oil-payment channel.
frame.conditions: The invoice specifies Dollars even though gold conversion is unavailable.
frame.atmosphere: A conceptual exam question tests whether the learner confuses backing with usefulness.

frame.process: Explain the material meaning behind the name Rupiya.

frame.when: Before tracing dated rupee milestones.
frame.conditions: A historical word origin does not establish modern backing.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a craftsperson shaping silver.

skipped_steps.why: This etymological fact contains no numerical quantity to scale.

frame.process: Trace common coin standards and the centralisation of currency issuance.
frame.how: Follow rulers, mints, laws, a gold-exchange bridge and the RBI.
frame.when: Proceed from 1540 through Mughal and Company stages to 1935, distinguishing the 1938 note issue.
frame.conditions: Separate physical standards, legal status, issuance rights and external monetary links.
frame.atmosphere: Markets spanning regions need recognisable payments under changing political authorities.

frame.process: Distinguish three historical coin names by metal.
frame.how: Match Mohur with gold, Rupee with silver and Dam with copper.
frame.when: After the colonial timeline and before explaining the silver crisis.
frame.conditions: Metal pairings do not supply weights or denomination ratios; biological layer and shape slots do not apply.
frame.atmosphere: Three labelled historical coins arranged for an examination matching exercise.

frame.process: Explain how increased silver supply could depress its price and trouble a silver-linked currency.
frame.how: Run a hypothetical bullion-market example, then connect it to the historical discoveries.
frame.when: The heading spans 1873–1947; the discoveries concern the late nineteenth century.
frame.conditions: Discoveries must increase actual or expected supply, and demand must not absorb that increase.
frame.atmosphere: Silver dealers face additional supply while external obligations involve gold-linked currencies.

frame.process: Trace independent India's changes in symbols, subdivisions and monetary arrangements.
frame.how: Use separate everyday transactions to distinguish decimal, fiat and exchange-rate concepts.
frame.when: Move through 1947–1957, the 1955 law, 1957 reform, 1971, 1993 and 2010.
frame.conditions: Political independence, design changes and monetary reforms need not occur simultaneously.
frame.atmosphere: Independent India changes its monetary framework while households continue paying in rupees.

frame.process: Compare the old subdivisions with the hundred-paise rupee.
frame.how: Build equal-value equations and derive smaller-unit relationships.
frame.when: Contrast the old system with the 1957 replacement.
frame.conditions: Old paise or pice are not modern decimal paise.
frame.atmosphere: A learner converts an old price and reads a modern price label.

frame.process: Explain intervention that moderates excessive exchange-rate movements.
frame.how: Add RBI dollar sales to a hypothetical foreign-exchange market.
frame.when: Intervention is relevant during excessive volatility, not at a stated automatic numerical trigger.
frame.conditions: The illustrative result holds other influences constant and guarantees no particular rate.
frame.atmosphere: An importer faces a sudden rise in the rupee cost of dollars.

frame.process: Define official digital currency expressed in Indian rupees.
frame.how: Transfer an illustrative wallet amount, then unpack status, form and unit.
frame.when: Introduce the 2022 milestone before its pilot segments.
frame.conditions: A digital payment interface or commercial-bank deposit is not automatically Digital Rupee.
frame.atmosphere: A participating shop accepts a rupee-denominated digital currency payment.

frame.process: Distinguish wholesale and retail Digital Rupee pilots.
frame.how: Compare bank-to-bank settlement with public purchases and explain gradual expansion.
frame.when: Clarify the wholesale November 2022 launch against the supplied October entry, then retail in December 2022.
frame.conditions: Pilot participation is limited and expands; no current participation total is supplied.
frame.atmosphere: Banks, merchants and users test an official digital currency in stages.

last_problems: [reviewer] b56; b59: “October 2022 entry” points to source wording instead of directly teaching the chronology. “यहाँ current participation count नहीं दिया गया है” similarly comments on supplied material rather than teaching the monetary system. -> fix: Teach directly: “Wholesale pilot 1 November 2022 को शुरू हुआ; October को launch month मत समझना।” Delete the participation-count sentence, retaining the distinction between gradual expansion and universal availability.

[reviewer] c15.3, b45–b47: The prescribed intervention example is split across the concept naming: b46 names volatility smoothing before b47 runs the $100 invoice costs and explains how dollar sales increase supply. The complete numerical mechanism therefore does not precede the term as S2-08 requires. -> fix: Before b46, run the demand shock, dollar-sale supply response and $100 cost movement ₹8,000 → ₹8,400 → ₹8,200. Then name and define volatility smoothing. Move rather than duplicate b47’s explanation, and shorten b49’s replay to preserve timing.

videos.title: Tughlaq की token currency: भरोसा कहाँ टूटा?

frame.process: Locate the introduction and subsequent failure of Tughlaq’s monetary experiment.
frame.how: A royal decision introduced brass and copper payments alongside the established silver reference.
frame.when: Introduction in 1329–1330 CE; breakdown and withdrawal follow, without an exact withdrawal date.
frame.conditions: Military and administrative needs faced scarce treasury silver.
frame.atmosphere: The Delhi Sultanate needs spending capacity while market acceptance remains essential.

frame.process: Explain token currency through a payment accepted at declared value.
frame.how: A hypothetical seller accepts a copper token instead of silver for the same basket.
frame.when: Example first, then definition, boundary and subsequent use.
frame.conditions: Recognised payment value is distinct from material value and requires acceptance.
frame.atmosphere: A hypothetical Sultanate grain bazaar.

frame.process: Compare silver and tokens, then historical tokens and modern fiat currency.
frame.how: Separate payment value, material, authority, safeguards and credibility.
frame.when: Compare the issue arrangement before explaining withdrawal and modern parallels.
frame.conditions: Declared equality does not establish equal metal value or guaranteed acceptance.
frame.atmosphere: Move from a grain payment to a treasury counter and present-day shops.

frame.process: Trace the need for tokens and the mechanism that undermined their use.
frame.how: Scarcity motivates issue; imitation and weak enforcement undermine authenticity and onward acceptance.
frame.when: Needs precede introduction; counterfeiting precedes rejection and withdrawal.
frame.conditions: Useful monetary expansion requires acceptance, authentication and effective control.
frame.atmosphere: A state financing expenditure and traders deciding whether payment can be trusted.

frame.process: Read the established-currency, breakdown and final-outcome labels accurately.
frame.how: Follow arrow positions and distinguish private refusal from treasury resource loss.
frame.when: Silver baseline, token introduction, loss of trust, then withdrawal and loss.
frame.conditions: The sequence supplies qualitative outcomes, not a numerical historical loss.
frame.atmosphere: An annotated historical flow and a conditional treasury example.

last_problems: [reviewer] b3–b7 before b8–b9; b20 before b22–b23; b6 before b29: Economics concepts के prescribed numerical examples उनकी पहली naming/explanation के बाद आते हैं। Tokens की बराबरी b3 में समझाई जाती है, जबकि basket example b8 में है। Counterfeiting b20 में नामित है, numerical mechanism b22–b23 में चलता है। Trust और control का निष्कर्ष भी उनके numerical demonstration से पहले दिया जाता है। -> fix: b2 के historical opening के तुरंत बाद b8 का basket चलाएँ, फिर token term और declared-value explanation दें। Failure को पहली बार समझाने से पहले b22 का 10 genuine/10 fake वाला run रखें। Modern trust comparison में b13 का पूरा onward-payment run पहले रखें। समय बचाने के लिए बाद के duplicated explanations और recaps हटाएँ, book content नहीं।

[reviewer] b5–b7, b19–b21, b28–b31, b34–b37: वही trust-collapse, withdrawal और material-versus-acceptance निष्कर्ष कई बार दोहरते हैं। Timeline में पूरा outcome पहले बताया जाता है, reasoning में फिर चलता है, और facts-label section तथा closing में फिर recap होता है। यह no-duplicate-recaps नियम तोड़ता है और teaching को आगे बढ़ाने के बजाय रोकता है। -> fix: Timeline में historical orientation रखें; detailed failure mechanism reasoning part में एक बार खोलें। Comparison recap में केवल comparison रखें। Facts section में arrows की evidence-reading और private refusal बनाम fiscal cost का नया फर्क रखें; एक ही final causal recap बचाएँ। बचा समय example-first rearrangement में इस्तेमाल करें।

[reviewer] b13: Prescribed modern-money example का दूसरा transaction narrated balances के बिना खत्म होता है: note प्याज वाले को जाता है, लेकिन shopkeeper का ₹100→₹0 और vegetable seller का ₹0→₹100 नहीं बोला जाता। -> fix: दोनों closing balance movements एक छोटे वाक्य में जोड़ें; b17 की दोहराई हुई onward-acceptance explanation घटाएँ।

videos.title: Note वापस लेना, demonetisation और Gresham's Law

frame.process: Demonetisation removes the affected notes' legal-tender status.
frame.how: Contrast an ordinary purchase before and after the legal cutoff.
frame.when: Example first, definition next, then a boundary test and historical application.
frame.conditions: Legal status must be removed; possession or printing changes alone are insufficient.
frame.atmosphere: A buyer holds the same paper note at a shop counter across a legal change.

frame.process: Track three demonetisations and the separate stages of the ₹2,000 note.
frame.how: Attach governments, denominations and legal consequences to dates.
frame.conditions: Do not infer motives or treat introduction, printing cessation and withdrawal as equivalent.
frame.atmosphere: Indian currency policy, including the need to supply cash after the 2016 change.

frame.process: Notes return from circulation without losing legal-tender status.
frame.how: Exchange one ₹2,000 note for four ₹500 notes and distinguish cash composition from legal standing.
frame.when: The 2023 withdrawal, following the timeline.
frame.conditions: The ₹2,000 notes retain legal-tender status.
frame.atmosphere: A note holder exchanges cash at a bank counter.

frame.process: Selective spending leaves lower-intrinsic-value money circulating while more valuable money is retained.
frame.how: Equal fixed payment values make spending cheaper material attractive; connect the illustration to Henry VIII's England.
frame.when: The holder chooses a coin at payment; repeated choices alter circulation.
frame.conditions: Both monies are legal tender, valuation is government-fixed, one is intrinsically undervalued and holders can choose.
frame.atmosphere: A hypothetical bazaar followed by the historical English silver-coin example.

frame.process: Compare good and bad money by intrinsic value, treatment and presence in payments.
frame.how: Read both sides together and show storage versus hand-to-hand circulation.
frame.when: After the spending mechanism and its conditions have been established.
frame.conditions: Shared legal payment value; good and bad do not mean genuine and counterfeit.
frame.atmosphere: A split comparison showing valuable coins stored or melted and cheaper coins spent.

beats.on_screen: Cheaper coin held 1 → 0; dearer coin held 1 → 1. Good coin available 1 → spent 0.

beats.on_screen: Same rice bag for either coin; buyer retains the more valuable metal. Name the law after the example.

beats.on_screen: Metal value ₹12 versus legal payment ₹10; fixed valuation under-rewards the valuable coin.

videos.title: UPI payment के पीछे कौन क्या करता है?

frame.process: Distinguish RBI's legal oversight from NPCI's institutional identity.
frame.how: Attach the legal year to the Act and the establishment year and founders to NPCI.
frame.when: The Act is dated 2007; NPCI was established in 2008.
frame.conditions: Not-for-profit does not imply that every service is free.
frame.atmosphere: A customer sees an app but depends on institutions behind it.

skipped_steps.why: No formula is present.

frame.process: Read the payment ecosystem as a role diagram.
frame.how: Move from RBI to NPCI, then across banks, payment apps and users.
frame.when: Read institutional layers before following a particular payment.
frame.conditions: Visible connectors show a schematic arrangement, not every transaction's route.
frame.atmosphere: A kirana customer and merchant use shared payment arrangements.

frame.process: Separate connecting infrastructure from customer-facing services.
frame.how: Move from NPCI's shared infrastructure to account providers, interfaces, gateways and merchants.
frame.when: These roles cooperate when an eligible customer makes a payment.
frame.conditions: Payments banks cannot lend; commercial and small finance banks can.
frame.atmosphere: A hypothetical ₹200 grocery checkout connects distinct service roles.

frame.process: Follow a UPI payment and a bounded delegated-payment arrangement.
frame.how: Authorise, submit, identify banks, verify funds, confirm and distinguish settlement; delegate permission before secondary-user spending.
frame.when: The payment experience takes seconds; delegated payments are associated with August 2024.
frame.conditions: Valid authorisation, available funds and applicable spending permission are needed.
frame.atmosphere: Rahul pays a shop and tea seller; a daughter buys groceries using her father's permitted funds.

frame.process: Locate each participant in the simplified UPI route.
frame.how: Read left to right through app, payer bank, switch and recipient bank, with RBI oversight behind them.
frame.when: These responsibilities apply during the illustrated payment.
frame.conditions: Routing is not deposit custody; confirmation is not interbank settlement.
frame.atmosphere: Freeze Rahul's successful payment to examine its components.

frame.process: Distinguish payer-initiated sending from authorised recipient-side collection.
frame.how: Compare a chosen tea payment with electricity collection under prior permission.
frame.when: Push begins with the payer's immediate choice; the illustrated pull uses earlier authority.
frame.conditions: Pull collection requires an authorised arrangement and its conditions.
frame.atmosphere: A tea stall and a household's monthly electricity bill.

last_problems: [reviewer] c26.3, b15–b18: The concrete ₹200 checkout runs after the banking categories, app, gateway and merchant have already been named and defined. This reverses the required economics example-first sequence. -> fix: Move the ₹200 purchase before the category explanations. Run the account, permission, checkout and receiving roles concretely, then attach their names and definitions. Replace b16's standalone list and shorten b19 to make room.

[reviewer] c27.1–c27.2, b23–b34; b39: The same route and institutional functions are taught and recapped repeatedly: walkthrough, route explanation, fast run, flow recap, another four-box walkthrough and another labelled recap. This breaches the explicit no-duplicate-recaps requirement. -> fix: Retain one complete process run and its required fast flow recap. Make c27.2 a genuinely distinct spatial inspection without repeating the full mechanism; consolidate b28, b34 and b39 rather than delivering three overlapping summaries.

[reviewer] b26–b27: “नया bank account खोलना नहीं बताया गया है” and “settlement का अलग exact time नहीं दिया गया” describe what the source does not say instead of directly teaching the distinction. -> fix: Say directly that secondary spending permission does not itself create a new deposit account, and that fast customer confirmation must not be equated with identical timing for interbank settlement. Replace the existing sentences without adding time.

[reviewer] c27.3, b38: The definition pattern ends with another identification recap, without explaining where the push–pull distinction will be used next. -> fix: Replace part of b38 with a brief forward application: when comparing payment arrangements, distinguish who initiates collection from the channel's speed or name.

last_problems: [reviewer] b2–b7, b9–b14, b29–b34: NEFT, RTGS and AEPS are named and assigned their mechanisms before their required numerical examples run. Even within the NEFT example, b11 names batching before completing the balance changes. This reverses the explicit example → term → definition sequence. -> fix: Open with the numerical NEFT and RTGS stories, complete each money movement, then introduce its term and service facts. Move AEPS naming until after the withdrawal and authentication example. Fund this reordering by removing repeated previews and recaps in b7–b8, b16–b17 and b31.

[reviewer] b5–b6, b19, b22–b25: Several comparison facts remain compressed lists rather than opened teaching. In particular, 'default' is never explained, Person-to-Merchant is not plainly defined, and the full-form beat does not explain what the names emphasise despite claiming p014-i8#q2. The amount comparisons mostly announce thresholds rather than showing the consequences across services. -> fix: Explain default as the ordinarily applicable starting limit and Person-to-Merchant as a person paying a business. Explicitly connect electronic transfer, gross settlement, immediate payment and interface to the four names. Run one amount-choice example across the relevant services, retaining all qualifications. Replace repeated use summaries in b24, b26 and b28 rather than adding duration.

[reviewer] b6–b7, b21, b23: Phrases such as 'comparison में', 'फिर मिलते हैं', 'बताए जाते हैं' and 'UPI figures ... हैं' report source wording instead of consistently teaching the facts directly. Conversely, conditional or source-specific fee and UPI figures are not clearly distinguished from independently verified current rules in the spoken narration. -> fix: Teach the operational distinctions directly without referring to a comparison or repeated wording. Put explicit source-status qualifications in non-spoken provenance labels for the printed fee and limit claims; retain spoken warnings against universal application. Replace the existing reporting phrases rather than lengthening these beats.

last_problems: [reviewer] b14–b17, c30.3: Debit, credit and prepaid are named before any worked example. Their funding definitions follow, but no numerical purchase is actually run for each type. This fails the required economics example-first sequence. -> fix: Run short hypothetical purchases before naming the types: spend ₹200 from a ₹1,000 linked account, borrow ₹200 repayable later, and spend ₹200 from ₹500 loaded value. Then name and define each type. Replace abstract repetitions in b16–b17 and shorten duplicate voucher recaps to fund the addition.

[reviewer] c30.3 frame and b15–b17: The classification claims common teaching slots but does not deliver them consistently. Only prepaid receives an explicit everyday image; naming reasons and comparable consequences are absent. Physical layer/shape/location slots are neither adapted nor explicitly skipped with a reason. -> fix: Use the same economics-relevant slots for all three: funding source, why named, spending timing, everyday image and consequence. Explicitly explain in skipped_steps why anatomical slots do not apply. Integrate these slots into the worked purchases rather than adding another recap.

[reviewer] b4, p015-i12: The credit-card-to-UPI concept is named before its mechanism is demonstrated. 'Interface UPI, funding credit' is accurate but remains an abstract distinction without the required numbered transaction example. -> fix: First show a hypothetical ₹300 merchant purchase initiated through UPI and funded by linked card credit, leaving a ₹300 repayment obligation rather than deducting ₹300 from the deposit account. Then name the linkage. Label this as an illustrative explanation, not an actual scheme amount. Cut repeated summary wording in b8 or b13.

[reviewer] b27, b32, b37–b41: The same restricted-voucher conclusion is repeatedly recapped. The process pattern justifies one fast run and one flow recap, but the additional conclusions repeat rather than advance the explanation. -> fix: Keep the required process run and flow recap; make c31.4 a brief application question testing authorised location and excluded uses. Remove duplicate unrestricted-cash conclusions and use the saved time for the missing worked examples.

videos.title: Cross-border payments, polymer notes और cryptocurrency

frame.process: Define Nexus as a BIS Innovation Hub-led connection between national fast payment systems.
frame.how: Follow a hypothetical India–Singapore remittance through separate domestic payment legs.
frame.when: Explain the intended arrangement, not an asserted live corridor.
frame.conditions: Currency conversion and applicable charges remain necessary.
frame.atmosphere: A sender in India wants to support a relative in Singapore.

frame.process: Identify the objective, founding participation and five country–system pairs.
frame.how: Associate each country with its own named national system.
frame.when: After defining the initiative and before explaining connection costs.
frame.conditions: Participation is distinct from leadership; ease is an objective.
frame.atmosphere: A country–system matching exercise anchored in familiar UPI payments.

skipped_steps.why: These are associations and an objective, with no formula to build.

frame.process: Explain intermediary costs and the benefit of shared connection standards.
frame.how: Add an illustrative handling stage, then contrast separate interfaces with a shared design.
frame.when: During remittance routing and payment-system integration.
frame.conditions: Fees and delays vary; connection standardization does not abolish currencies or legal requirements.
frame.atmosphere: A bank transfer counter and a payment-integration desk.

frame.process: Define polymer notes by their supporting material.
frame.how: Replace cotton-based paper with security-grade BOPP while retaining face value.
frame.when: A hypothetical authorized note is used in a purchase.
frame.conditions: The example does not establish Indian circulation.
frame.atmosphere: A kirana purchase worth ₹10.

frame.process: Distinguish engineered banknotes from ordinary plastic and coexistence from withdrawal.
frame.how: Compare security design and the treatment of existing paper notes.
frame.when: When interpreting a proposed material change.
frame.conditions: A different substrate alone neither creates a banknote nor cancels existing currency.
frame.atmosphere: A shopkeeper checks notes and keeps valid paper notes in use.

frame.process: Interpret proposed denominations and the lifespan multiplier.
frame.how: Compare a baseline lifespan with an upper-bound multiplier.
frame.when: When assessing the proposed small-denomination introduction.
frame.conditions: Up to 4x is not an exact outcome or four extra years.
frame.atmosphere: Frequently handled ₹10 and ₹20 notes.

frame.process: Place international introduction and Indian trial approval in chronological order.
frame.how: Move from Australia in 1988 to Government approval in 2013.
frame.when: Distinguish introduction, approval and wider adoption.
frame.conditions: Approval is not proof of nationwide circulation; adoption figures have no supplied reference date.
frame.atmosphere: International experience alongside a limited Indian testing proposal.

frame.process: Explain durability, anti-counterfeiting and replacement-cost objectives.
frame.how: Reduce illustrative unfit notes, then separate wear resistance from imitation resistance.
frame.when: Over comparable periods of handling and replacement.
frame.conditions: Illustrative quantities are not measured savings; objectives are not achieved outcomes.
frame.atmosphere: A bank cash counter collecting worn notes.

frame.process: Define cryptocurrency through a blockchain-recorded digital transfer.
frame.how: Track changes in hypothetical holdings and explain linked records.
frame.when: After a transfer is validated.
frame.conditions: Fees are ignored in the illustration; digital form does not establish official monetary status.
frame.atmosphere: Two users transferring a hypothetical digital asset.

frame.process: Separate privately created crypto from RBI-issued digital money.
frame.how: Compare issuer and legal-tender status rather than digital appearance.
frame.when: When classifying an asset as official money or a private asset.
frame.conditions: Absence of legal-tender status alone does not determine legality of holding or trading.
frame.atmosphere: Two digital balances with different institutional status.

frame.process: Explain ownership recording through a distributed ledger.
frame.how: Validate a proposed transfer and update records maintained across participating computers.
frame.when: A valid transfer is accepted under network rules.
frame.conditions: An unaccepted instruction does not establish changed ownership; network details vary.
frame.atmosphere: Several computers maintain a consistent ownership record.

frame.process: Explain distrust and payment grievances as motivations for alternatives.
frame.how: Trace mortgage default to loss, and a merchant fee to lower net receipts.
frame.when: During financial distress or costly and incompatible payment experiences.
frame.conditions: Motivation proves neither crypto safety nor freedom from fees; crisis losses do not prove dollar purchasing-power erosion.
frame.atmosphere: A hypothetical US mortgage lender and an Indian kirana payment counter.

[reviewer] c35.2, b55–b59: The comparison names Digital Rupee but explains issuer and legal-tender status explicitly only for crypto. The recap table's values are not supplied, so both sides of the comparison are not actually taught. -> fix: Explicitly state that Digital Rupee is RBI-issued and legal tender, whereas the private crypto described here is neither. Populate both columns. Replace the repeated screen-appearance warning in b56 or the generic recap in b59 to preserve timing.

[reviewer] b13–b14: Narration describes aligned cells and numbered rows instead of directly teaching the country–system associations. videos.title: Money supply: M0 से M4 तक क्या गिना जाता है?

frame.process: Define the economy's money holdings at an instant.
frame.how: Transfer ₹100 between two holders, then distinguish the unchanged stock from payments.
frame.when: Measure at one selected instant, not across a month.
frame.conditions: Specify eligible monetary components and avoid repeated counting.
frame.atmosphere: A buyer pays a neighbourhood kirana shop.

frame.process: Organize the five aggregate names by coverage.
frame.how: Keep M0 separate; branch M2 and M3 from M1 and extend M3 to M4.
frame.when: Overview precedes detailed formulas.
frame.conditions: Overlapping aggregates must not be added together.
frame.atmosphere: A household and shop hold cash and several kinds of deposits.

frame.process: Read and qualify the five-tier money pyramid.
frame.how: Scan apex to base, then replace misleading cumulative implications with component baskets.
frame.when: After the family overview and before detailed mechanisms.
frame.conditions: Printed abbreviations are not complete definitions.
frame.atmosphere: Five widening tiers beside an accurate branch diagram.

frame.process: Money moves through payments and deposits.
frame.how: Follow a household payment to a shop and its bank, with a separate bank–RBI link.
frame.when: During purchases, wages, deposits and lending.
frame.conditions: A payment generally transfers money; every household payment need not directly involve RBI.
frame.atmosphere: A local shop connected to the banking system.

frame.process: Identify directly RBI-created reserve money.
frame.how: An RBI security purchase credits a bank's reserve account.
frame.when: Central-bank money provides a base for subsequent banking activity.
frame.conditions: Reserves support settlement and potential lending, not compulsory lending.
frame.atmosphere: RBI and a commercial bank's reserve account.

frame.process: Construct M0 from three monetary stocks.
frame.how: Distinguish circulating currency, other RBI deposits and bankers' RBI deposits.
frame.when: Use balances for the same instant.
frame.conditions: Use common units; include bank vault cash and CRR balances without double counting.
frame.atmosphere: Public wallets, a bank vault and accounts held at RBI.

frame.process: Bank lending creates deposit money across the banking system.
frame.how: An ₹80 loan and a subsequent ₹60 loan create ₹140 of deposits under stated assumptions.
frame.when: Lending and interbank settlement occur in successive rounds.
frame.conditions: Reserves, capital, liquidity, lending standards and credit demand constrain expansion.
frame.atmosphere: Two banks, a business borrower and a supplier.

frame.process: Define M1 through near-immediate spendability.
frame.how: Demonstrate a cash purchase and a demand-account payment before explaining Narrow Money.
frame.when: Funds are needed for everyday transactions.
frame.conditions: Almost immediate use does not mean every form of savings qualifies.
frame.atmosphere: A customer paying for groceries.

frame.process: Build M1 and M2 component by component.
frame.how: Add public currency, demand deposits and other RBI deposits; then add eligible post-office savings deposits.
frame.when: Compare updated balances after completed transfers.
frame.conditions: Exclude bank vault cash from public currency and NSC from the M2 addition.
frame.atmosphere: Wallet, bank account and post-office passbook.

frame.process: Classify post-office products as included or excluded in the M2 addition.
frame.how: Separate savings-bank deposits from NSC and similar instruments.
frame.when: Before adding post-office holdings to M1.
frame.conditions: Product type, not the institution alone, determines inclusion.
frame.atmosphere: Two different savings products offered at a post office.

frame.process: Compare liquidity and convenience of savings deposits.
frame.how: Contrast availability of funds with ease of accessing or using them.
frame.when: A saver needs money for a payment.
frame.conditions: Relative inconvenience does not imply inaccessibility; no current restrictions are assumed.
frame.atmosphere: A saver comparing bank and post-office account access.

frame.process: Construct M3 and M4 and distinguish importance from breadth.
frame.how: Add bank time deposits to M1, then qualifying post-office deposits to M3.
frame.when: Use same-date stocks; reset assumptions for separate worked examples.
frame.conditions: M3 does not start from M2; M4 excludes NSC and counts post-office savings once.
frame.atmosphere: A bank FD conversion, a monetary-statistics desk and a news headline.

frame.process: Explain RBI monitoring and the NSC exclusion.
frame.how: Trace loan-created deposits into monetary indicators, then contrast spendable cash with a long-term certificate.
frame.when: Policy analysis compares monetary growth with credit, output and prices.
frame.conditions: M3 is an indicator, not proof of inflation; specific exclusions do not exclude all term deposits.
frame.atmosphere: A local business loan and a family's long-term savings decision.

last_problems: [reviewer] b6–b9, b11–b15, b26–b27, b41–b44, b55–b59: Aggregate names, component definitions and formulas precede the required numerical examples. The later examples cannot satisfy S2-08 retrospectively. In particular, the overview names the whole family before running its supplied holdings-and-transfer example. -> fix: Run the supplied hypothetical holdings and numerical movements before assigning aggregate names, then attach definitions and real-life links. Move the existing calculations forward and cut repeated overview/formula recaps rather than adding another example sequence.

[reviewer] c37.2 b26–b30; c38.2 b43: OD is expanded only as 'eligible दूसरे RBI deposits'. This substitutes an unexplained eligibility label for its meaning. The account-holder/institution boundary is not concretely demonstrated, although OD is a component of both M0 and M1. -> fix: Contrast a bank's RBI account, an eligible other institution's RBI account, and a customer's commercial-bank account. Use the supplied standard OD example with an outside label and clarify that not every non-bank RBI balance automatically qualifies. Replace part of the repeated M0 recap to make room.

[reviewer] c39.1 b55–b59; c38.1 b39: Bank time deposits are mainly illustrated by FD and RD labels, but their defining agreed-term condition is never clearly taught. 'उसकी शर्तें आ सकती हैं' does not explain what distinguishes them from demand deposits or why they are less payment-ready. -> fix: After the numerical conversion, explicitly explain that a time deposit is held for an agreed period and early access may carry conditions; contrast this with withdrawal on demand. Replace a repeated importance/breadth statement rather than extending the video.

[reviewer] c38.4 b50–b54: The comparison largely repeats 'fairly liquid but less convenient'. 'Access का रास्ता आसान होना' rephrases convenience without giving the learner an image or mechanism, so this book line remains insufficiently opened. -> fix: Use a clearly hypothetical payment situation showing that funds can be withdrawable while accessing or using them involves an extra arrangement. last_problems: [reviewer] c40.1 b2–b6; c40.2 b7–b10; c41.1 b14–b18; c41.2 b19–b21: The required example-first sequence is reversed. Public blockchain and ledger control are named and explained before the 0→10 sacks and rejected 10→20 example runs. RTGS, NEFT and settlement are likewise defined and compared before the ₹2,00,000 example. Even within that example, RTGS is named before the alternative batch route finishes. The maker's claim that examples precede the mechanisms is therefore not consistently true. -> fix: Run each complete numerical scenario first in plain language, then attach the technical names, definitions and real-life link. For blockchain, show the accepted 10 sacks and rejected overwrite before naming the shared-ledger mechanism. For transfers, run both alternative routes and balance changes before naming RTGS and NEFT, then present the comparison. Move existing beats rather than adding narration; cut duplicated recaps b6/b12 and b18/b24 if transitions need time.

frame.process: Payment infrastructure can turn account ownership into usable financial access.
frame.how: A hypothetical cross-bank household transfer makes funds available for household needs.
frame.when: Access and linked accounts come first, followed by authorisation, successful transfer and use.
frame.conditions: Participating accounts, connectivity, affordability and user capability matter; infrastructure alone cannot guarantee inclusion.
frame.atmosphere: A worker in a town sends household money to a family member in a village.

frame.how: Distinguish the shared card-payment arrangement from the bank account holding the customer's funds.
frame.when: The institutional relationship is checked before selecting the statement combination.
frame.conditions: A card scheme and a bank account have different roles.
frame.atmosphere: A customer uses a RuPay-branded card at a shop terminal.

beats.say: अब खुद जाँचिए: किसी गाँव में payment व्यवस्था आ गई, तो क्या हर व्यक्ति उसका इस्तेमाल जरूर करेगा? नहीं, access और इस्तेमाल कर पाने की शर्तें भी चाहिए। दुकानदार को reward मिला, तो क्या वह acceptance charge है? नहीं; claim कितना बड़ा है और पैसा किस दिशा में गया, यही पकड़िए।
beats.on_screen: Transfer check: payment facility ≠ guaranteed use; reward received ≠ acceptance charge. Check claim scope and money direction.
